questions.question: In British India, which one among the following Acts permitted detention without trial for up to two years ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act, 1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Rowlatt Act of 1919**, officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, authorized the government to detain individuals without trial for a maximum period of two years.
 
• This act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council during the Viceroyalty of Lord Chelmsford.
 
• The act aimed to curb revolutionary activities and maintain order in British India following World War I.
 
• It allowed for the arrest of individuals suspected of sedition without requiring any formal trial or evidence.
 
• The act faced widespread opposition, including the launching of nationwide protests led by Mahatma Gandhi, which culminated in the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** in April 1919.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:** On 13th April 1919, General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering in Amritsar, killing hundreds and injuring thousands. This incident intensified the opposition to the Rowlatt Act.
 
• **Gandhi's Role:** Mahatma Gandhi initiated the **Rowlatt Satyagraha** in response to the act, marking one of the first nationwide protests against British rule.
 
• **Sedition in British India:** The act was part of a broader strategy to suppress dissent and revolutionary activities, particularly against organizations like the **Ghadar Party** and other freedom movements.
 
• **Repeal of the Act:** The widespread protests and opposition eventually led to the act becoming largely ineffective, although it was never formally repealed during British rule.
 
• **Historical Significance:** The Rowlatt Act and the subsequent protests highlighted the growing demand for self-rule and the increasing discontent with British colonial policies.

questions.question: The "Khudai Khidmatgar" (Servants of God) was founded by -
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

• The **Khudai Khidmatgar** was a non-violent movement founded by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (also known as Frontier Gandhi) in 1929 in the North-West Frontier Province (now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan). ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***

• The movement was known for its discipline, emphasis on social service, and promotion of unity among Pashtuns.

questions.question: Hunter Commission of 1919 was constituted to examine which of the following incidents?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hunter Commission was constituted in 1919 by the British government to investigate the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**.
 
• The massacre took place on **13 April 1919**, when British troops under General Reginald Dyer fired on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab.
 
• Approximately **379 people were killed** and over 1,000 were injured in the incident, though unofficial estimates suggest much higher numbers.
 
• The Hunter Commission was led by **Lord William Hunter**, a former Solicitor-General for Scotland.
 
• The Commission's findings were widely criticized as biased, as it failed to hold General Dyer fully accountable for the atrocities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:**

 
 
• The massacre is considered a turning point in India's struggle for independence.
 
• On the day of the massacre, people had gathered peacefully to protest against the **Rowlatt Act**, which allowed the British to detain Indians without trial.
 
• General Dyer ordered troops to open fire without warning and blocked the main entrance to prevent escape.
 
• The incident led to widespread outrage and condemnation both in India and internationally.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act:**
 
 
• Passed in 1919, the Rowlatt Act extended wartime emergency measures to suppress revolutionary activities.
 
• It allowed the British government to imprison suspects without trial and curtail civil liberties.
 
• The act sparked nationwide protests, leading to events like the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.
 
 
 
• **Impact on National Movement:**
 
 
• The massacre intensified anti-British sentiments and mobilized Indians for independence.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest against the incident.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi launched the **Non-Cooperation Movement** in 1920 as a response to British atrocities.
 
 
 
• **General Reginald Dyer:**
 
 
• Known as the "Butcher of Amritsar," Dyer defended his actions, claiming it was necessary to instill fear.
 
• He was criticized by some in Britain but received support from imperialists.
 
• Dyer was relieved of duty but faced no severe consequences for his actions.

questions.question: Who is know as the 'father of all India services'?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** is known as the '**father of all India services**'.
 
• He played a crucial role in the **formation of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** and the Indian Police Service (IPS).
 
• Patel was India's first **Deputy Prime Minister** and **Minister of Home Affairs**.
 
• His efforts were instrumental in integrating the **princely states** into the Indian Union after independence.
 
• He is also referred to as the '**Iron Man of India**' for his determination and strong leadership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lal Bahadur Shastri**__

 __
 
• **Lal Bahadur Shastri** was the **second Prime Minister** of India.
 
• He is known for the slogan "**Jai Jawan Jai Kisan**" and his role in the **Green Revolution**.
 
 
 
• **J. B. Kripalani**__
 __
 
• **J. B. Kripalani** was a prominent **Indian freedom fighter** and politician.
 
• He served as the **President of the Indian National Congress** during the transfer of power in 1947.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**__
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the first **Prime Minister of independent India**.
 
• He is known for his vision of a modern India and his contributions to **nation-building**.

questions.question: What was the secret society of revolutionaries organised by VD Savarkar in 1904 known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhinav Bharat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Abhinav Bharat** was a secret society of revolutionaries founded by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar** in 1904.
 
• Initially named **Mitra Mela**, it was later renamed Abhinav Bharat in 1906 to align with its revolutionary objectives.
 
• The society aimed to overthrow British rule in India through armed struggle and foster a sense of national pride and unity.
 
• Abhinav Bharat inspired many young revolutionaries, such as Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad, who later became prominent figures in India’s freedom movement.
 
• The society was eventually disbanded in 1952, but it played a significant role in the early years of India's struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (VD Savarkar):**

 
 
• Known as **Veer Savarkar**, he was a freedom fighter, writer, and a key figure in India's revolutionary movement.
 
• He authored the book **"The First War of Indian Independence"**, which highlighted the 1857 rebellion as a national uprising.
 
• He was also a strong proponent of Hindutva ideology, which sought to unite Hindus culturally and politically.
 
 
 
• **Mitra Mela:**
 
 
• This was the original name of Abhinav Bharat, established by Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar.
 
• Mitra Mela initially focused on cultural and social reforms before transitioning into a revolutionary organization.
 
 
 
• **Revolutionary Activities:**
 
 
• Abhinav Bharat members engaged in activities like distributing nationalist literature and organizing secret meetings.
 
• They also plotted and executed attacks on British officials, such as the assassination of British officer W.C. Rand in Pune by Chapekar brothers.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Abhinav Bharat:**
 
 
• The organization’s emphasis on self-reliance and armed resistance influenced future revolutionary groups like **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).**
 
• Despite its dissolution, the spirit of Abhinav Bharat remains an integral part of India's freedom struggle narrative.

questions.question: Which festival did Tilak introduce in 1893 to promote a sense of unity and nationalism?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ganpati Festival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ganpati Festival**, also known as **Ganesh Chaturthi**, was introduced by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** in **1893**.
 
• Tilak popularized this festival to promote a sense of **unity and nationalism** among Indians during the British colonial rule.
 
• He transformed the festival from a private family celebration into a **public event** to unite people across caste and religious lines.
 
• The festival became a platform for spreading **social and political awareness** and fostering the spirit of **Indian independence**.
 
• Tilak’s efforts made the Ganpati Festival a **symbol of cultural pride** and a tool for **mass mobilization** against British oppression.
 
• The celebration includes **public processions**, **cultural performances**, and the installation of **Ganesh idols** in public spaces.
 
• Even today, the festival holds great significance and is celebrated with grandeur, especially in the state of **Maharashtra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Holi Festival**__

 __
 
• **Holi** is a Hindu festival celebrating the arrival of **spring**, the victory of **good over evil**, and the festival of colors.
 
• The festival has no historical association with promoting nationalism or unity during the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Shivaji Festival**__
 __
 
• The **Shivaji Festival** was also introduced by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** to honor the legacy of **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj**.
 
• It symbolized **Maratha pride** and was used as another tool to inspire nationalism and resistance against the British.
 
• However, it was not introduced in **1893**, and its primary objective was to celebrate Shivaji’s achievements, not to unify people through a festival like Ganpati.
 
 
 
• **Diwali Festival**__
 
 
• **Diwali**, the festival of lights, is a major Hindu festival symbolizing the victory of **light over darkness** and **good over evil**.
 
• It has deep **mythological significance** but was not associated with Tilak’s efforts to promote unity or nationalism.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the extremists?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitutional reforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The extremists within the Indian National Congress primarily demanded **Complete Swaraj** (self-rule).
 
• They advocated for the **Promotion of Swadeshi industries** to reduce dependency on British goods and promote Indian businesses.
 
• The goal of **Complete independence** from British rule was a core demand of the extremists.
 
• In contrast, **Constitutional reforms** were not a primary demand of the extremists, as they sought more radical changes than merely constitutional adjustments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extremists in the Indian National Congress**

 
 
• Led by figures like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
• They believed in direct action and mass mobilization to achieve self-rule.
 
• Extremists used methods such as boycotts, Swadeshi movements, and passive resistance.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement**
 
 
• Part of the larger Indian independence movement aimed at promoting Indian goods and boycotting British products.
 
• Started in response to the partition of Bengal in 1905 by Lord Curzon.
 
• Encouraged self-reliance and the revival of domestic industries.
 
 
 
• **Moderates vs. Extremists**
 
 
• Moderates believed in gradual reforms and constitutional methods to achieve self-governance.
 
• Extremists demanded immediate self-rule and were willing to use more aggressive tactics.
 
• The split between moderates and extremists became evident during the Surat session of the Indian National Congress in 1907.
 
 
 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905)**
 
 
• Implemented by the British to divide and rule by separating the largely Muslim eastern areas from the largely Hindu western areas.
 
• Led to widespread protests and was a significant factor in the rise of extremist activities.
 
• The partition was eventually annulled in 1911 due to the intense opposition.
